tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: For crisp panel lines, use RB Productions' scribing tools. First, lightly score the panel lines with the pencil tip, then deepen them with the scriber. For deeper lines, use the 0.5mm scriber for visible panels and the 0.3mm for finer details. Work slowly and apply even pressure. Afterwards, gently sand with 5000 grit sandpaper to remove burrs. This technique works perfectly on kits like ICM's Il-2 Shturmovik.

tips.title: Photo-Etch Bending with Eduard's Bending Jigs
tips.text: Eduard's photo-etch bending jigs allow you to create complex shapes without warping. Apply super glue to the photo-etch part, place it in the jig, and press gently until set. For intricate parts, use a combination of jigs. After bending, clean up any excess glue with a hobby knife. This method is ideal for Arma Hobby's complex Pz.IV H decal set.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata's Air-Cleaner
tips.text: Regular cleaning of your Iwata airbrush needle maintains optimal performance. After each session, backflush with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner and let it soak for 10 minutes. Then, use Iwata's Air-Cleaner kit to clean the needle under magnification. Use the smallest brush provided to scrub the needle's tip, then rinse with thinner and dry with a lint-free cloth. Regular cleaning prevents clogging and ensures consistent paint flow.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Tamiya tape is ideal for masking large, flat surfaces due to its width and self-adhesive backing. For intricate details, use Kabuki tape's narrow width and precise cutting capabilities. To switch between tapes, use a hobby knife to score the edge of the tape and carefully peel it off. For complex shapes, use a combination of both tapes. This technique is useful when applying different colors to a single panel, like on the Tamiya 1/48 Tomcat.

tips.title: Sanding Stick Progression with Tamiya Sanding Sticks
tips.text: For smooth surfaces, use Tamiya sanding sticks in a progression of grits. Start with 400 grit to remove mold seams, then progress to 800 and 1000 grit for a smooth finish. Wet-sand using water and a suitable lubricant like Tamiya Extra Thin Cement as a substitute for water. Sand in one direction, then switch to a perpendicular direction for the next grit. Always rinse and dry the surface between grits to avoid scratching. This technique works well on large, curved surfaces like the wings of the Trumpeter Su-27 Flanker.
